cases.description: HTML in a heading contributes the text between its tags, and the anchor element is removed before trimming (step 1, decisions C13 and C15): `## Title one ` gives `title-one`; GitHub gives `title-one-`, since it keeps the space next to the anchor element (decision C13).

Headings holding only an anchor element with an id, one with a class only, or an HTML comment have empty slugs and no derived anchor, while the explicit anchor `o` and the tag `only` are listed (§6.2, decision C14); GitHub gives the first the anchor `""` and the others no permalink.

An anchor element with content is a structural error, so `anchors` fails as `parse` does, with `anchor-element-invalid` on the section (§5.1, §6.2); GitHub gives the heading `title-ten-inner-text`.

An anchor element whose id breaks the name pattern is a validation error (`anchor-invalid`, §6.2), so the record stays readable and lists the explicit anchor `a.b_c-d`, and the heading gives `title-thirteen`; GitHub gives `title-thirteen-`, since it keeps the space next to the anchor element (decision C13).

The explicit anchor `later-heading` of one heading and the derived anchor `later-heading` of a later one are both listed, although `check` reports them as a duplicate anchor (§6.1, decision C16), and the first heading gives `first-has-anchor`; GitHub gives `first-has-anchor-`, since it keeps the space next to the anchor element (decision C13).

HTML in a heading contributes the text between its tags, supported or not, so `## <script>alert(1)</script> script words` gives `alert1-script-words` (step 1, §5.3); GitHub gives `scriptalert1script-script-words`, since its sanitizer keeps the tags as text.

HTML in a heading contributes the text between its tags, and the anchor element is removed before trimming (step 1, decisions C13 and C15): `## <notatag> words` gives `words`; GitHub gives `-words`, since it keeps the space left by the removed HTML.
HTML in a heading contributes the text between its tags, and the anchor element is removed before trimming (step 1, decisions C13 and C15): `## <b>escaped</b> words` gives `bescapedb-words`.

The explicit anchor `earlier-heading` and the derived anchor of the heading before it are both listed, although `check` reports them as a duplicate anchor (§6.1, decision C16), and the second heading gives `third-has-anchor`; the first heading, `## Earlier heading`, is added to the captured case, where GitHub gave the second `third-has-anchor-`, since it keeps the space next to the anchor element (decision C13).

`check` reports the derived `later-heading` of the second heading as a duplicate of the explicit `later-heading` on the first (§6.1, decision C16), and the second section key `later-heading` as a duplicate key, the first key being the anchor (§5.5, §5.7).

`check` reports the explicit `earlier-heading` of the second heading as a duplicate of the first heading’s derived `earlier-heading` (§6.1, decision C16), and the second section key `earlier-heading`, its anchor, as a duplicate key (§5.5, §5.7).
